questions.question: When you see the Tram Only command sign, which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding other vehicles and road use?

options.text: All vehicles must stop and wait for the tram to pass before proceeding.
Only trams are allowed to travel beyond this point or lane; other vehicles must not enter.
Bicycles and motorcycles are allowed to share the tram lane.
Pedestrians have the right of way over trams on this road.

questions.question: While driving on a road, you see the following road sign: a blue circle with a white border and the number “60” inside. Which of the following best describes the legal instruction associated with this sign?

options.text: You must not exceed 60 km/h under any circumstances.
You are legally required to drive at least 60 km/h unless traffic or road conditions make it unsafe.
This sign only applies to vehicles driving in the fast lane.
The speed shown is recommended when road conditions are poor.

questions.question: You are driving a heavy duty truck that has a gross vehicle mass (GVM) of 11.5 tons. You encounter a blue circular sign with a white border and the number “10t” inside. How must you legally respond to this sign?

options.text: Continue driving at any speed below 10 km/h as long as you're being cautious.
Drive in the part of the road that is indicated by that sign.
Avoid entering the road altogether because your vehicle exceeds the limit.
This sign only informs you that your truck's mass must not exceed 10 tons to proceed.

questions.question: You are approaching a temporary roadworks site at night. A blue circular road sign with a white arrow pointing diagonally to the left is mounted on a traffic barrier. There are no cones or flag personnel visible. What does this sign legally require you to do?

options.text: You must pass to the left of the obstruction unless you are driving an emergency vehicle.
You may pass on either side of the obstruction if the road appears clear.
You are legally required to keep to the left side of the sign, regardless of traffic conditions.
The sign serves only as a warning of an upcoming construction and can be ignored at night.

questions.question: You are driving on a dual carriageway during early morning traffic when you encounter a road maintenance vehicle partially blocking the left lane. A blue circular road sign with a white arrow pointing to the bottom right is fixed on the rear of the obstruction. What are you legally required to do?

options.text: You must reduce speed and pass the obstruction on either side, depending on traffic.
You may pass to the right or left, provided no traffic officer is present.
You are legally required to pass to the right of the obstruction, even if the left lane appears open.
You must stop and wait for traffic to clear completely before proceeding.

questions.question: You're approaching an intersection and see this command sign (blue circle with a white arrow pointing to the left). Which of the following is the correct course of action?

options.text: You may turn left or go straight ahead, depending on traffic.
You must stop completely before deciding which direction to take.
You are legally required to proceed left only, as no other direction is permitted.
You must give right of way to oncoming traffic before turning right.

questions.question: You see this sign while driving (a blue circle with a white arrow pointing right). What does it instruct you to do?

options.text: You may go straight or turn right.
You are only allowed to proceed in the direction of the arrow, to the right.
Turning right is optional if no traffic is coming.
You must stop and give way before turning right.

questions.question: What does this road sign instruct drivers to do?

options.text: You must turn left or right at the next intersection.
You may continue straight or turn if the road is clear.
You are only allowed to proceed straight ahead.
You must stop and wait for further instruction.

questions.question: You see this sign at an upcoming T-junction. Your GPS tells you to turn right, and there are no physical barriers blocking that direction. What must you do?

options.text: Follow the GPS and turn right carefully if there are no other vehicles.
Proceed straight across the junction since no stop sign is present.
Ignore the sign if there’s no traffic officer present and go right.
Obey the sign and turn left, even if your GPS instructs otherwise.

questions.question: You’re approaching a controlled intersection with this sign displayed at the turn. There’s a green traffic light and no oncoming traffic. A side road to the left is open and seems clear. What is the correct and legal action?

options.text: Turn left if you're familiar with the area and there's no traffic.
Continue straight ahead if there’s no physical barrier.
Turn right as instructed, regardless of what the traffic light or side road conditions show.
Wait for a traffic officer to confirm if the turn is allowed.

questions.question: You're driving in an unfamiliar city and approach a narrow pathway marked with this sign. The GPS suggests it's a shortcut to your destination, and there are no visible pedestrians at the moment. What must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly and proceed if no pedestrians are present.
Drive through carefully since it's a suggested shortcut.
Stop, check for pedestrians, and proceed only if safe.
Do not enter, this path is legally restricted to pedestrians only.

questions.question: You’re driving on a road with a "Pedal Cycles Only" sign, and you notice that there are no cyclists in sight. The road appears clear, and it leads to a faster route that could save time. What is the legal and safe course of action?

options.text: Drive through the area at a very low speed, as there are no cyclists.
Continue driving if it seems empty, and assume the sign doesn’t apply to cars.
Stop and check for any cyclists before proceeding, ensuring it’s safe.
Do not enter or drive on this road at all, as it is exclusively for pedal cycles.

questions.question: You are a delivery driver in a residential area and your navigation suggests a shortcut through a path marked with a “Pedal Cycles and Pedestrians Only” sign. You notice a wide, paved path ahead with no barriers. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed slowly and carefully since the path is wide enough and seems empty.
Proceed only if you switch on your hazards and yield to any pedestrians or cyclists.
Do not use the path at all, as it is strictly for pedal cycles and pedestrians.
Use the path, but only during daylight hours and under 20km/h.

questions.question: You are riding a 125cc scooter and approach a path marked with a “Motorcycles Only” command sign. Your friend, who is riding a quad bike, wants to follow you through the same path. What is the correct course of action?

options.text: Proceed normally, and allow your friend on the quad bike to follow since it's similar to a motorcycle.
Proceed, but tell your friend to wait, as only two wheeled motorcycles are allowed.
Wait for your friend to catch up, since quad bikes fall under the same class of vehicles.
Take an alternate route, as scooters are not allowed on motorcycle only paths.

questions.question: You are RIDING A MOTORCYCLE. You approach a road with a “Motor Cars Only” sign. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed, as motorcycles are similar in size to motor cars.
Stop and turn around, as the sign excludes all vehicles except passenger motor cars.
Proceed only if your motorcycle is a superbike.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
